column1: # Claude's two passes (QUALITY.md end) for Morning Word declarations (English, God's Word door, KJV pasted by code).

column3: Each declaration is the listener's own first-person response to the verse, never God speaking and never a promise God did not make: verses that carry a promise (PSA 37:4, PSA 37:5, LUK 1:45, ISA 65:24, PRO 11:25) are answered with trust and practice, not with an outcome; no health, wealth or sleep claims; repentance and forgiveness kept honest (1JO 1:9, LUK 15:20, PSA 86:5); Hagar named with dignity (GEN 16:13). Faithful to each passage; a deacon board could read any of them aloud.
column5: Plain warm first person for a woman starting her day: ordinary work (dishes, a shift, paperwork, the phone and the news), the young ones watching, laughter, loneliness and family named without pity. Anti-AI read: openings and sentence shapes varied across the 90 days (repeated frames and the big-ones-and-small-ones list rewritten), no filler words, no exclamation marks, no em dashes; every day 15-25 s spoken.

column3: First-person response to each verse, never God speaking and never a promise God did not make: promise verses (MAT 6:33, PSA 31:24, PSA 112:7, PSA 29:11, MAT 5:4) answered with trust and practice, not outcomes; grief, fear and bad news named honestly without a fix promised; forgiveness and no-condemnation kept faithful to the text (ROM 8:1, EPH 4:32, MAT 5:44 as one small step, not pressure). No health, wealth or sleep claims; nothing a deacon board would wince at.
column5: Warm plain first person for a working woman starting her day (traffic, the counter, the phone, the kitchen table); mothers and Mary named with tenderness; small humour kept. Anti-AI read: the I-do-not-have-to frame (used 15 times across 91-365) rewritten into varied shapes, openings varied, no filler words, exclamation marks or em dashes; every day 15-25 s spoken.
